correctness.rationale: For each of the four possible geometries of two selected cells, the exact probability follows from independent paired row/column choices, giving the finite covariance factorization. Distinct nonattacking cells have independent statuses; attacking tuples constitute O_r(1/m+1/n) of tuples, with every nonzero joint probability bounded by (1+O_r(1/m+1/n))/(mn)^r. This proves all marked factorial moments and independent spatial Poisson limits. The common argmax payoff-refresh probability follows from conditional integrations and tends to q/(2-q). The standalone script passed 224 exact finite assertions, not used as an infinite proof.

A general unlocated coupled-random-map theorem might nonetheless subsume it.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Additive perturbation need not reproduce retained-coordinate replacement. A joint large-action Poisson overlap limit cannot be inferred from fixed small-game cases, nor from a theorem about correlation of distinct players’ payoffs in one game. In particular the exact covariance is a product of cross-copy agreement coefficients and the persistence intensity specializes to (q/(2-q)) squared. This requires distinct proofs; potential broader uninspected general results remain a priority risk.

evidence: The paired choice-map formulation is equivalent to two coupled random generic bimatrix best-response maps when players’ payoff matrices are independent and continuous. Mimun et al. (2022), arXiv:2209.12967, instead explicitly correlate player payoffs within one game.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: One must not equate payoff correlation between players with coupling of two copies in time. In the former the equilibrium mean depends on player-payoff correlation; here each game has exactly unit equilibrium mean for every retention probability, while the cross-copy covariance factorizes. Hence the inspected in-game correlation theorem cannot imply the present paired-copy result.

originality.rationale: The exact cross-version equilibrium covariance and three-population marked spatial Poisson theorem apply to two independently-payoffed games coupled across time. The inspected classical literature treats one-game counts or in-game payoff correlation, neither of which determines coupled-game overlap. The additive perturbation study does not give the rank-resampling result. A broader historical paired-random-map theorem not yet located remains a documented risk.

value.rationale: This separates equilibrium persistence from new equilibrium creation even though each version always has expected count one. The nontrivial exact correlation product quantifies two-player agreement and the spatial Poisson split calculates survival, loss, birth and simultaneous no-equilibrium probabilities. For half retention, only 1/9 common equilibrium is expected asymptotically; this is mathematically motivated stability calibration for ordinal games.
